If you don't have the time to answer this, that's fine, but I usually understand concepts better having someone tell me rather than just googling: what is the rule of thirds?

You don't have to read the article, the pictures are fairly self explanatory: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rule_of_thirds

Divide an image into a grid of 9 squares and try to align features in the photo with the imaginary grid i.e. the horizon lines up with the bottom third or the upper two thirds of the grid, objects such as a tree or an animal line up with the intersection of two lines.

You might have noticed that some digital cameras come with a feature that overlays a grid on the screen - this is what it's for.

EDIT: As an example, here's one of my own: https://slimgur.com/images/2015/06/23/833e4596c22341349d9692a4187a2699.jpg Horizon at bottom third, tree at roughly bottom-right line intersection.
